submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires only on the final 't' of an n't negation contraction spelled with the curly Unicode apostrophe (’, two byte tokens), strongest for present-tense do-support 'don’t'/'doesn’t' after a pronoun subject (I/We/She, ~0.7-0.9 of max) and weaker after noun subjects or for didn’t/haven’t/aren’t (~0.2-0.4), near zero for won’t/isn’t/weren’t/imperative 'Don’t', and zero for wasn’t/couldn’t, for the bare ’ or other ’ contractions (’s, ’m), and for uncontracted 'do not'. The ASCII apostrophe ('t, at most ~0.1) and the apostrophe-less ' dont' (~0.2) give only weak activation.
